text:
Few players in the league have been unluckier than Charlie Coyle this season. He is a 20-minute center in Columbus, and the Blue Jackets are winning his minutes: 56.8% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 12 points better than without him. The goals have not followed.

He has 3 goals on 6.0 expected, shooting 6.5% against a range of 10.4% to 14.9% for him, and his team has scored 11.7 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. That is why his 14 points in 20 games look ordinary, and why our wins added, which credits goals at the moments they swing games, ranks him 527th of 548 skaters. Process and results have rarely pulled this far apart.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season (90th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists) who gets to the home-plate area in front of the net. Evolving-Hockey had him 58th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement. Our range for his season is 52 to 76 points, middle 63. Goals tend to follow chances like these, which is what we would watch.
